**Navigation, not truth.** Every column is read from an authority and every
description is a link rather than a summary. If you want to know how a feature
behaves, open its doc; if you want to know whether it is healthy, open Mission
Control. Nothing is restated here, on purpose — a second copy of a description
is a second thing to keep true.

| Authority | What it owns |
| --- | --- |
| `memory/registry.yml` | which files and runtime keys belong to a feature |
| the mapped feature doc | how that feature behaves now |
| `src/lib/admin/feature-registry.ts` | the runtime `FeatureKey` vocabulary |
| `memory/incidents/**` | confirmed defects |
| `memory/operations/release-queue.yml` | repair units in flight |

## Runtime keys with no semantic owner

A key that nobody owns is *said* to be unowned. Leaving it off every list
would be indistinguishable from an oversight, which is the whole failure this
reconciliation removes.

- `integrations` — **platform**. Inngest job execution. Infrastructure that carries other features' work, not a product feature with behaviour of its own to document.
